source.title: Wideband Up-Converting Mixer for Digital Communications Implemented in 130nm CMOS Technology (MASc thesis, G. Patulea, Carleton University, 2015)
source.figure: Fig. 4.12 (PDF 99): one Gilbert cell of the I/Q up-converter (switching quad T1/T3/T8/T9, baseband pair T10/T11, tail T6, baseband bias divider RP0-RP3, decoupling CV0-CV2)
source.inputs: source/ (thesis PDF, figures, metrics_sizing.xlsx, operating_conditions.xlsx, pvt_corners.xlsx, cadence_schematic.png; see source/ORIGIN.txt)
modifications: dut_benchmark.scs = final.scs plus RD_P (VDD RF_P) and RD_N (VDD RF_N) at the thesis value (owner answer PT2a: the thesis's hand-calculated drain load, eq. 68 PDF 90; the chip's peaking inductors and active balun are not in the netlist). RD is the sizing variable R_D. 2026-10-24 (owner): plus a top-level `parameters W_SW W_BB W_T` line declaring the per-finger widths (variables.yaml). final.scs itself is unchanged.

Devices: the thesis is IBM 130 nm (L = 120 nm); the dataset netlist uses sky130 01v8 nfets at L = 0.15 um with the thesis widths/fingers (rule D7: exported devices kept, biases re-chosen by simulation).

VSS.provenance: rule G3: DUT ground pin without a family role, held at 0 V

TAIL_BIAS.provenance: rule D7: tail T6 gate voltage re-chosen by simulation for the thesis's 2 mA tail current (PDF 89) in sky130 (thesis 465 mV, Fig. 4.12, leaves the sky130 tail nearly off); sizing variable V_TAIL

op_check.note: All seven devices are meant to be saturated at the quiescent point (thesis 4.3.2-4.3.3, PDF 88-90: tail, baseband pair and the switching quad checked for saturation); at the DC point both LO pins sit at the LO DC level, so the quad is balanced.

known_issues: Up-converter in a down-conversion family: the baseband input (20 MHz) is the family's RF input and the quad drains (output at f_LO + f_BB = 5.02 GHz) the IF output; the mixer_*_sb_v1 recipes measure the upper sideband (sideband: +1, owner answer PT4a).

Single-cell scope (PT1a): the thesis's simulated and measured numbers are for the complete I/Q chip (two cells, CML phase shifter, active balun); the targets are the thesis's single-cell values (hand calculations, sections 4.3.3-4.3.5). Chip-level metrics (I/Q gain 3.74 dB, sideband suppression, output P1dB/OIP3 at 1/2.4 GHz, chip power) are not covered.
Baseband drive AC-coupled (PT3a, recipe setting rf_dc_block_F): the DUT's own divider RP0/RP1 and the 1.03 kOhm resistors RP2/RP3 set the baseband gate DC level.

Supply (rule D7): the thesis chip runs at 2.0 V (above the sky130 1.95 V rating); the task uses 1.8 V, the thesis's hand-design supply (PDF 90) and one of its measured points. The measured supply sweep 1.8/2.0/2.2 V (PDF 119) reports only complete-chip current/power and clock sensitivity, no single-cell metric, so the task has the nominal condition only (rule D3).

The LO DC level is not given for the single cell (Fig. 4.12 annotations ~1.58-1.69 V at 2 V; hand design minimum 1.0 V): it is the sizing variable V_LO (testbench drive level lo_bias_V), re-chosen by simulation (rule D7).
